title: Temporal display shaders: E-Ink, Playdate crank and Game Boy LCD
blurb: A live scrolling HTML reader drawn through one WebGL 2 canvas with ping-pong feedback framebuffers. Switch between E-Ink Carta partial-refresh ghosting with a full black flash, a 1-bit Playdate screen with a draggable rotary crank, and a 4-shade olive Game Boy DMG-01 LCD with slow pixel persistence.
question: Can a WebGL 2 ping-pong feedback shader give live interactive HTML real temporal hardware screen behaviour (E-Ink partial-refresh ghosting and full black flash, 1-bit Playdate crank scrolling, and 4-shade Game Boy DMG persistence) that stateless CSS filters cannot express?
result: Not verified in a live browser yet. One ElementGL canvas uploads the scrolling reader with texElementSubImage2D(), feeds each frame through two ping-pong RGBA8 framebuffers to keep ghosting and LCD persistence across updates, renders the bezel and Playdate rotary crank in WebGL, and syncs hit testing with updateElementGeometry().
